# Assembly mass, CG and inertia — computed from placement

**Generated by `mechanical/assembly-v0/assembly_v0.py`. Do not
hand-edit — re-run it.**

> [!warning] Nothing here has been weighed or measured
> Every mass below is a retail listing or a reasoned estimate.
> **MEASURED appears nowhere**, because it would not be true of
> a single number in this document. What changed versus the
> existing chain is not the quality of the inputs — it is that
> the inertia is now computed from where the parts ARE, rather
> than from a frame mass multiplied by an invented 1.4x.

## Centre of gravity

`(0.12, -0.26, 1.14)` mm, relative to the top face of the bottom
plate. x and y are near zero by construction — the layout is
symmetric — and that is a **weak** confirmation, not a strong
one: a symmetric model of an asymmetric vehicle would also
report a centred CG.

## Inertia about the CG

Point-mass model: each component is treated as its mass at its
centre. That omits each part's own spread about its own centre,
so these are a **lower bound**, not an estimate with error bars.

| axis | this model | derivation chain | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ixx | 0.00583 | 0.00541 | +7.7 % |
| Iyy | 0.00581 | — | — |
| Izz | 0.01085 | 0.01060 | +2.3 % |
| AUW | 1129.8 g | 1390.0 g | -18.7 % |

### What that comparison actually says

**The AUW is 18.7 % lower and the inertia is within 7.7 %.**
Those two facts together are the interesting result, and they
are not a coincidence: rotational inertia is dominated by the
four motors out at r = 175 mm, and the motor mass is one of the
better-sourced numbers in the project (a real listing for the
exact chosen part). The chain's **AUW** error lives mostly in
terms near the centre — the invented frame multiplier and the
invented misc mass — which barely move inertia at all.

So the gains derived from that chain are less wrong than the
AUW gap suggests. **They are not retuned here**, and this is
not an argument that they should be: a point-mass model built
from listings is not grounds to move a gain. Gains wait for
measured thrust (B2).

## Still not measured

- **R3**, the 1.4x printed-vs-CF multiplier, is bypassed here
  rather than corrected: this model computes the printed frame's
  mass from its own solids. The multiplier is still INVENTED
  wherever else it is used.
- **R9**, the 30 g misc mass, is replaced by explicit fastener,
  wiring and standoff terms — all three ESTIMATE.
- The receiver, antenna, buzzer and their placements are
  envelopes for parts nobody has chosen. They reserve space; they
  do not describe hardware.
